nbinom.title: Negative binomial distribution
nbinom.section1.title: Definition
nbinom.section1.intro: The negative binomial distribution describes the number of failures before a fixed number of successes in independent Bernoulli trials with the same success probability.
nbinom.section1.scenarios: It can model the number of unsuccessful attempts before a target number of successes.
nbinom.section1.rel1: Each trial has two possible outcomes.
nbinom.section1.rel2: The trials are independent and the success probability is constant.
nbinom.section1.rel3: The geometric distribution is the special case with one required success.
nbinom.section2.title: Probability mass and cumulative distribution
nbinom.section2.pdf: The probability of \(k\) failures before \(r\) successes is \(P(X=k)=\binom{k+r-1}{k}p^r(1-p)^k\), for \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\).
nbinom.section2.cdf: The cumulative distribution function is \(P(X\leq k)=\sum_{j=0}^{k}P(X=j)\).
nbinom.section2.param_note: Here \(r\) is the required number of successes and \(p\) is the success probability.
nbinom.section3.title: Plots
nbinom.section4.title: Properties
nbinom.section4.usage: Useful for counts of failures before a target number of successes.
nbinom.section5.title: R functions
nbinom.section5.desc: R provides functions for probabilities, cumulative probabilities, quantiles, and random generation.
nbinom.section5.code:
dnbinom(x, size, prob)
pnbinom(q, size, prob)
qnbinom(p, size, prob)
rnbinom(n, size, prob)
nbinom.section5.paramNote: In R, size is the target number of successes and prob is the probability of success.
